newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends flat, central bank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends flat, central bank intervenes.

text.p: The won closed flat against the dollar on Thursday as the central bank stopped the dollar's slide stemming from exporter settlements and fund inflows for equity investment, dealers said.
"Heavy dollar positions weighed on the market. But the central bank bought dollars at 887.00 level to ease pressure on dollar unwinding," a foreign bank dealer said.
Dealers estimated the central bank's dollar buying at $200 to $300 million.
The won ended at 887.20, unchanged from Wednesday's closing. It opened at 887.50 and moved between 886.80 and 887.60.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 887.20 on Friday, compared with 887.40 today.
"But the central bank's intervention was weaker, raising suspicion that the bank may allow the dollar to fall below 887.00," said the foreign bank dealer.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 886.50 to 887.50 on Friday.
But a trade surplus in June and rising foreign exchange holdings would continue putting downward pressure on the dollar for the time being, they said.
